is_anopheles.evidence: Studied Anopheles coluzzii collected from Takatsaba village, Tessaoua Department, Niger (Page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotyped Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and L1014S (L995S) mutations using TaqMan assay (Page 5, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (Page 7) reports exact genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for L1014F in permethrin-alive (n=55) and permethrin-dead (n=19) An. coluzzii.

african_field_population.evidence: Indoor-resting blood-fed Anopheles females collected in Takatsaba village, Tessaoua Department, Maradi State, Niger in September 2017 (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field collection, bioassay, and molecular genotyping study.

sub_country_location.evidence: Takatsaba village, Tessaoua Department, Maradi State, Niger (13.7559°N, 7.9865°E) (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Field sampling conducted specifically for this study in September 2017.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay data are reported in Table 1 and Figure 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study collected indoor-resting Anopheles coluzzii in Takatsaba, Niger in September 2017. Bioassays revealed high resistance to pyrethroids and DDT, and TaqMan genotyping of 74 F1 females (55 permethrin-resistant survivors and 19 dead) showed a high frequency of the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) mutation (81.8% in survivors vs 36.8% in dead), significantly associated with permethrin resistance.
